notes: Phase 5 fixtures for docs/sales-agent-implementation-plan-ru.md. Each fixture exercises src.ai.sales_response_prompts.sales_response_prompt + src.ai.sales_response_models.SalesResponseOutput only -- no SalesPolicyEngine, no persistence, no real business, no message delivery. `approved_move` in every fixture plays the role of the server's already-made, binding decision: the generator's ONLY job is to phrase it. allowed_knowledge_ids/business_fact_ids/customer_evidence_ids are always derived by the eval script from each fixture's own knowledge_cards/business_facts/customer_evidence lists -- an id-injection fixture supplies a narrow allowed set on purpose so a model output that reaches outside it is a checkable failure, not something only a human reviewer could catch. v2: every fixture now supplies exactly ONE non-null fallback string for its approved_move (handoff_template only for HANDOFF_TO_HUMAN, safe_fallback_text otherwise) -- scripts/sales_response_generation_eval.py's _check() now asserts, for every fixture uniformly, that message_text is byte-for-byte equal to that string whenever the model itself sets used_safe_fallback=true or move=HANDOFF_TO_HUMAN (see check_fallback_text_is_exact in src/ai/sales_response_models.py), matching src/engine/sales_response_validator.py's own exact-match rule instead of the earlier, incorrect 'closely paraphrase' contract. v2 also adds fixtures for unconfirmed price, waived fee/complimentary, refund promises, premature booking/payment confirmation, self-assigned callback, a plain STOP (no emergency wording), a plain emergency (no STOP wording), a knowledge id claimed from a different tenant/turn, a customer quote offered in place of a real evidence id, an unconfirmed business fact, and a customer trying to talk the model into a move other than approved_move.
